Haudenosaunee

The Haudenosaunee Confederacy, also known historically as the Iroquois Confederacy, brings together the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga, Seneca and Tuscarora nations. The Onondaga Nation’s public account explains how the Grand Council connects these nations and why its council fire is at Onondaga.

01

Identity and context

Haudenosaunee is the name of a confederacy connecting the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga, Seneca and Tuscarora nations. It is a broader political relationship, rather than another name for one constituent nation.

Read the sources [1] haudenosauneeconfederacy.com

02

03

The Six Nations and the Council Fire

The Onondaga Nation describes a shared council established to maintain peace among the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca. The Tuscarora joined later, in the early eighteenth century. In the Nation’s account, chiefs and clan mothers have responsibilities in Confederacy government. The Grand Council gathers at Onondaga, where the Nation keeps the Central Fire. Its public account describes the Longhouse as a place for council, cultural and community life.

Read the sources [4] Onondaga Nation

04

Homelands in present-day New York

Fort Stanwix National Monument traces the original alliance across present-day New York, from Mohawk communities in the lower Mohawk Valley to Oneida in the upper valley, Onondaga near Syracuse, Cayuga in the Finger Lakes and Seneca in the Rochester–Buffalo region. The individual nation guides link to sources on their particular communities and the places described in those sources.

Read the sources [5] National Park Service · Fort Stanwix National Monument

05

The American Revolution

The Fort Stanwix account describes early efforts to stay out of the war, followed by divisions within and among the six nations. Many Oneida and Tuscarora supported the Americans, and many others sided with Britain. These differing choices help explain why records from individual nations and communities matter when reading about the Confederacy during the Revolution.

Read the sources [5] National Park Service · Fort Stanwix National Monument
